english.title: Use body for anatomical examination without registration - Human Tissue Act 2004

additionalkeywords.additionalkeyword: Births and Deaths Registration Northern Ireland Order 1976

english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) did an activity to which section 1(3) of the Human Tissue Act 2004 applied without the death of the person concerned having been registered under either section 15 of the Births and Deaths Registration Act 1953 or Article 21 of the Births and Deaths Registration (Northern Ireland) Order 1976
english.legislation: Contrary to section 5(5) and (7) of the Human Tissue Act 2004.

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
Section 5(6) of the Human Tissue Act 2004 provides that the offence does not apply where the person reasonably believes
(a) that the death of the person concerned has been registered under either of the above mentioned provisions OR
(b) that what he did was not an activity to which section section 1(3) of the Act applies.

other.penalty:
Summary: A fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: Three years imprisonment and/or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
